chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: The Regal stage show; leaving for the Grand Terrace in 1931
summary: Describes the band doing stage presentations behind chorus girls and acts, under M.C. Fess Williams.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, before we get into Earl, you say Peyton's band played in the pit and on the stage?
Yeah, on the stage it was under the direction of -- oh, I can't think of his name. He was an M.C.
Half Pint Jaxon?
No. You'd know him soon as I could think of the name. Oh, Fess Williams.
Oh, Fess Williams? Yeah.
Fess Williams, yeah.
Charlie Mingus's uncle.
Yeah.
Fess Williams. Interesting man. What'd you play on stage?
Oh, well, we had a show. You know, regular show.
You had a stage show?
Yeah. Chorus girls and everything. Acts.
Did the band do anything?
Yeah, we did band numbers. Did a couple band numbers. Called stage presentation.
What would the band do when they had a spot?
Oh, specialty numbers, you know. Special arrangements.
Were there-- guys take solos?
Yeah.
Like a jazz arrangement?
Just like a jazz arrangement, yeah.
How long were you at the Regal?
I was at the Regal about -- almost a year.
What is that --
I left the Regal in March, '31, went down to the Grand Terrace.
Well, you were telling me that's where Earl heard you?
I think so, yeah.
Did you know him before then?
I don't remember knowing Earl before that.
